inputs.sbc_source: 10-K FY2025 (filed 2026-02-25, accession 0001193125-26-071966): Note 18 Stock-Based Compensation, total SBC expense $1,307M (RSUs $1,282M incl. $394M one-off HPS/GIP incentive-retention awards, options $25M); MD&A liquidity discussion states $326M of employee tax withholdings related to employee stock transactions for 2025 (financing activities, distinct from the $1,951M 'Shares/Subco Units repurchased' cash-flow line). Combined SBC-incl-equity-taxes = 1,307 + 326 = 1,633. No single combined figure is published, so both lines are summed per the method's fallback rule. UPDATE 2026-11-19: 9M 2026 SBC expense $911M (10-Q Q3 2026 cash-flow statement) and employee tax withholdings $389M (statement of changes in equity); FY2026E ~ $1,200M + ~$400M = ~$1,600M, ~5.5% of ~$29.2B revenue, which anchors sbc_pct_path year 1.
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-10-31 (10-Q Q3 2026 cover) plus Q3 2026 diluted-EPS table
inputs.wacc_rationale: 8.0% built from a ~4.1% 10Y UST risk-free rate plus a ~5.5% US equity risk premium scaled by BLK's moderate-beta profile (asset manager with high operating leverage to markets but a diversified, recurring-fee, technology-subscription revenue base that dampens beta relative to a pure capital-markets business); no leverage adjustment needed given BLK's net debt is small (~$1.3B) relative to its ~$170B market cap. UPDATE 2026-11-19: unchanged. Net debt remains ~0.3% of market cap. Per-scenario WACC differences (7.0/8.0/9.5) are a prior judgment deliberately carried over; note they charge scenario risk in both the flows and the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: not material -- BlackRock's office leases are small relative to a $24B revenue, high-margin fee business; no separate lease line modelled (implicitly inside opex/EBITDA margin).
inputs.nci_treatment: Owner FCF is built off consolidated operating income and revenue, which include NCI - CIPs (consolidated investment products) and NCI - Subco (BlackRock Saturn Subco, the HPS all-equity-deal vehicle). Net income attributable to BlackRock, Inc. common shareholders is materially lower than consolidated net income once these are deducted, but the CIPs/Subco consolidation nets to roughly zero economic effect on a per-share basis because (a) CIP NCI represents non-recourse fund-level entities BlackRock does not own, largely self-funding and immaterial to enterprise FCF, and (b) Subco NCI (the ~7.6M Class B-2 units issued as HPS deal consideration) is captured by including the Subco units in the fully diluted share count used as the divisor. No separate NCI deduction is applied to the FCF bridge; the Subco dilution is handled entirely through the 163.156M fully diluted share count.
inputs.notes: UPDATE of the 2026-09-26 valuation, not a rebuild. Model unchanged: owner-FCF DCF, component route (SKILL.md routing: BlackRock is an operating asset manager -- fee revenue on AUM is operating revenue and corporate debt is real debt; not a bank/REIT/LIC row). fy0 stays FY2025 (base_revenue 24,216); year 1 = FY2026 and is now anchored on nine months of actuals (10-Q Q3 2026) rather than a forecast. WHAT CHANGED: (1) Anchors -- price, 2026-09-30 balance sheet, 2026-10-31 share count. (2) Contingent consideration, omitted by the prior version, is now charged: $5,858M liability in equity_bridge plus 2.8M fixed Subco Units in the share count. (3) Year-1 growth 10% -> 20.5% base (9M revenue $21,534M, +25% YoY; Q4 estimated ~$7.7B: base fees ~$6.1B on $15.5T AUM, technology ~$0.6B, performance fees ~$0.5B, distribution/advisory ~$0.5B => FY2026E ~$29.2B). (4) METHOD FIX -- the prior ebitda_margin_path was GAAP EBITDA (operating income + D&A), which is already AFTER SBC expense, and the engine then deducted sbc_pct_path again; year-1 implied EBIT margin was 22.9% against a FY2025 GAAP operating margin of 29.1%. ebitda_margin_path is now pre-SBC (GAAP operating income + D&A + SBC expense) so SBC expense is charged once and the employee-tax withholdings (cash, not in opex) are the only incremental deduction. (5) Margin, SBC%, D&A% and cash-tax paths re-anchored to FY2026E actuals: 9M GAAP operating income $7,603M = 35.3% of revenue (contingent-consideration marks net to only $26M over 9M), D&A $1,151M = 5.3% (of which intangible amortization $829M), SBC expense 4.2%, => pre-SBC EBITDA ~44.8%. The margin recovery the prior base spread over ~6-7 years arrived in year 1. (6) Bear year-2 growth 2% -> -4%. WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT UNCHANGED: growth years 2-10 in base and bull, and bear years 3-10 (would move on a change in organic base-fee growth away from ~9-10% or a market drawdown that persists into FY2027 averages); the terminal margin judgments -- base GAAP-EBITDA 42%, bull 46.5%, bear 35%, now expressed pre-SBC as 45.4/49.5/39.1 (would move if FY2027 adjusted operating margin guidance departs from '45% or greater', or on further impairments/extended retention grants); SBC% terminal 4.5/4.0/5.5; D&A% from year 5; capex 1.6/1.5/1.8% (9M actual 1.5%); terminal cash-tax 24/23/26; WACC, terminal growth and cap multiples; weights 20/50/30; hurdle 15%. Terminal D&A (3.0%) above capex (1.6%) perpetuates a small amortization tax shield (~1% of terminal value) -- carried over, flagged. CONVENTION NOTE: year 1 (FY2026) is discounted a full year from the valuation date although ~10.5 months have elapsed, while net debt is at 2026-09-30 after 9M of FY2026 cash generation was largely distributed ($2.8B dividends, $1.8B repurchases/withholdings); the full-year over-discounting (~6% of value) outweighs the ~$40/share of 9M cash counted in both places, so the net effect is conservative. FCF cross-check: last_fcf/reported_fcf remain FY2025 GAAP figures, which include -$3,536M of CIP operating cash flows; excluding CIPs FY2025 OCF was $7,463M and 9M 2026 was $6,915M (10-Q non-GAAP reconciliation). 9M 2026 owner FCF ex-CIPs = 6,915 - 316 capex - 389 withholdings - 911 SBC = ~$5.3B with Q4 seasonally the strongest quarter, against a model year-1 owner FCF of ~$8.4B (28.7% margin); the model sits at the upper end of that cross-check, mostly because cash taxes have run above book. Interest income is not stripped (net debt ~zero; unchanged).
inputs.share_count_basis: 166.93M = 154.423M common outstanding at 2026-10-31 + 7.607M Subco Units (10-Q cover: 162.030M 'fully diluted') + 2.1M treasury-method dilution from nonparticipating RSUs (1.7M) and options (0.4M) per the Q3 2026 diluted-EPS reconciliation + 2.8M FIXED HPS contingent-consideration Subco Units reclassified from liabilities to nonredeemable NCI on 2026-07-01 (subject only to post-closing conditions, excluded from reported diluted EPS). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows. The remaining variable earn-outs (GIP 4.0-5.2M shares; HPS up to a further 1.6M units) are NOT in the count -- they are deducted at their $5,858M balance-sheet fair value in equity_bridge, so each claim is charged once.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 cash-flow line 'Shares/Subco Units repurchased' was $1,951M but that line INCLUDES the $326M of employee tax withholdings (equity statement: $1,374M + $251M NCI-Subco = $1,625M of actual repurchases + $326M withholdings). buyback_cash is therefore 1,625, not 1,951; the prior version read the two as distinct. 9M 2026: $1,839M on the cash-flow line = $1,450M repurchases (1.3M shares/equivalents) + $389M withholdings. Guidance: at least $550M per quarter. BlackRock is a funded repurchaser -- the flat count is paid for in cash.
inputs.net_debt_note: Borrowings $12,740M less corporate cash $12,090M (= $12,877M consolidated cash less $787M held by consolidated investment products, which the 10-Q states BlackRock generally cannot access) = $650M net debt at 2026-09-30. The prior version used consolidated cash including $461M of CIP cash. Seed/co-investments are not credited and interest/dividend income is not stripped (unchanged matching treatment).

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS and owner-FCF CAGRs are not usable growth proxies for BLK over this window: FY2025 diluted GAAP EPS fell 15.6% YoY (driven by the one-off acquisition/impairment/contingent-consideration charges and a step-up in the diluted share count from Subco unit issuance for the HPS deal, not operating deterioration), while reported FCF and owner FCF both compress the same year for the same reason. Shareholders' equity CAGR (14.0%) is elevated by the HPS all-equity acquisition currency (BLK issued ~$12.8B of stock/Subco units for HPS in July 2025), so it overstates organic compounding. Revenue CAGR (10.65% over 3yr, but 18.67% in the latest year alone, boosted by AUM step-ups from GIP/Preqin/HPS consolidation) is used as the primary anchor for the growth path, moderated down in the scenario build below because a meaningful share of FY2025's revenue growth is inorganic (M&A) rather than organic AUM/fee growth, which management itself reports separately at ~10%.

base.narrative: Base case: FY2026 lands at ~$29.2B revenue (+20.5%: HPS/Preqin annualization in H1, record AUM of $15.5T, ~$869B TTM net inflows) with a pre-SBC EBITDA margin of ~44.8% (GAAP operating margin ~35.4%). From that higher base revenue growth follows the prior path -- 9% in FY2027 (about 5pp of which is the Q4 2026 run-rate carry-in) decelerating to 4% -- and the margin is HELD at the FY2026 level through year 6 before edging to the unchanged 42% GAAP-EBITDA maturity level (45.4% pre-SBC): management guides adjusted operating margin '45% or greater', but FY2026 is struck at record markets with a performance-fee line management itself warned not to extrapolate, so no further expansion is credited mid-path. SBC incl. withholding taxes glides from 5.5% to the prior 4.5% terminal as HPS/GIP retention grants roll off; D&A falls from 5.3% as acquired intangibles amortize; the cash tax rate starts at 26.5% (book amortization is largely non-deductible -- 9M deferred tax benefit $229M -- so cash tax on EBIT runs above the 24% normal rate) and reaches 24% by year 6. Working capital capture stays zero.

bull.narrative: Bull case: GIP/Preqin/HPS integration is a clean success; private credit, GAIIP AI-infrastructure fundraising and Aladdin (technology revenue +14% YoY) compound at double-digit rates, retirement-channel private-markets adoption opens a new AUM pool, and net inflows hold near the ~$869B TTM pace. Growth years 2-10 are unchanged from the prior bull (13% stepping down to 5.5%) off the higher FY2026 base -- FY2026 itself already outran the prior bull's year 1 (14%), so no extra growth is added. Margin expands from 45.0% pre-SBC to the unchanged 46.5% GAAP-EBITDA endpoint (49.5% pre-SBC), i.e. 'mid-to-high 40s adjusted margin is not a ceiling' proves out at the full-year level.

bear.narrative: Bear case: FY2026 is the high-water mark. Roughly $0.9T of the $1.45T AUM increase in 9M 2026 was market/FX rather than flows, and a sustained equity/bond drawdown takes it back: revenue falls 4% in FY2027 (changed from +2% -- on a base marked to record markets, +2% was no longer a downturn; -4% restores the prior ~18% cumulative three-year revenue gap to base) and then grows 1-2%. Fee compression in index/ETF persists, private-credit fundraising slows with the credit cycle and the AI-infrastructure trade, a Fink/Kapito succession stumble and talent attrition follow the three-deal integration, and retention grants are extended (SBC back to 6.0%). Margin de-levers from 44.7% to 39.1% pre-SBC -- the unchanged 35% GAAP-EBITDA endpoint, below the FY2022-23 trough of ~37.5% -- and the cash tax rate stays elevated.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 lands ~$29.2B revenue (+20.5%) at ~44.8% pre-SBC EBITDA margin -- the margin recovery arrived years early. Growth then follows the prior path (9% decelerating to 4%); margin is held flat through year 6 at a level struck in record markets, then edges to the unchanged 42% GAAP-EBITDA maturity level.
scenario_narratives.bull: Clean integration; private credit, AI infrastructure (GAIIP) and Aladdin compound at double digits; record inflows persist; margin expands to the unchanged 46.5% GAAP-EBITDA endpoint as 'not a ceiling' proves out.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY2026 is the peak: a market drawdown takes revenue down 4% in FY2027 then 1-2% growth; fee compression, slower private-credit fundraising, succession and talent risk; margin de-levers to the unchanged 35% GAAP-EBITDA endpoint, below the FY2022-23 trough.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED at 20/50/30 (house default 15/50/35 with 5pp moved from bull to bear). Bear 20%: no solvency risk, but the bear axis is single and well-precedented (a capital-markets drawdown mechanically hits AUM-based revenue, as in 2022) and FY2026 revenue is now marked to record markets. Base 50%: FY2026 is nine-twelfths actual and the path beyond it credits no further margin expansion. Bull 30%: still needs several distinct things to go right at once (private-credit and AI-infrastructure fundraising, three-deal integration, record inflows persisting, margin beyond guidance). The new evidence since September -- a Q3 beat flattered by one hedge fund's performance fee, and no named successor to Fink -- cuts both ways and does not move the weights; a named succession plan or a full year of 46%+ adjusted margin would argue for shifting 5pp back to bull.

valuation_philosophy.summary: BlackRock is valued as an operating company on owner free cash flow, not with a bank/REIT-style capitalization: fee revenue on AUM is operating revenue and the balance sheet carries real corporate debt, not deposits. The September judgment was that FY2025 margins were an acquisition-distorted trough; nine months of FY2026 confirmed it faster than modelled (GAAP operating margin 35.3% vs 29.1%, revenue +25%). The central judgment now is the opposite one: how much of FY2026 -- struck at record AUM of $15.5T with a flattering performance-fee quarter -- is repeatable. The base case accepts the FY2026 level but credits no further margin expansion for six years; the bear case treats FY2026 as a peak. Two claims the prior version missed are now charged: the $5.9B of stock-settled acquisition earn-outs, and SBC is charged once rather than twice.
key_risks_to_valuation: AUM/revenue is directly exposed to market levels; FY2026 base revenue is marked to record markets, so a drawdown hits a higher base (bear: -4% revenue in FY2027)

Terminal values bind differently by scenario: base and bull hit the 20x/22x cap, bear is Gordon -- base value is therefore insensitive to terminal growth but fully sensitive to the year-10 margin (45.4% pre-SBC)
Year-1 owner FCF (~$8.4B) sits at the upper end of the ex-CIP cash-flow cross-check (~$7.9B run-rate); cash taxes running above book for longer than the 26.5% -> 24% ramp would lower value
Contingent consideration ($5.9B, Level 3) rises with the share price and with GIP/HPS fundraising success -- it is a claim that grows in the bull case
Performance fees (~6% of revenue) are lumpy; Q3 2026 was flattered by one hedge fund with a Q3 measurement period
Fee compression in the index/ETF core, political/SIFI risk and CEO succession are not separately modelled beyond the bear path
Per-scenario WACC (7.0/8.0/9.5) is carried over from the prior version and widens the bear-bull spread beyond what the flows alone imply
